a1.title: Order pricing engine
a1.status: 6 of 6 golden tests · JaCoCo 100% on the pricing domain · PIT detected 185 of 185 mutations
a1.quote: An endpoint that receives the cart and returns the breakdown: per line and totals. Levers may coexist. Define and document the order of application and why that order is right. The quoted total and the confirmed total must be identical. No floating-point arithmetic for money.
how: `POST /api/v1/quotes` receives the cart and returns every line (gross, discounts with their origin, combo share, taxable base, rate and tax) and the totals, with the gifts and their quantity.
A **pure** pricing domain: no Spring and no JDBC, and an architecture test bans `float` and `double`. Money is `BigDecimal` with each country's scale and rounding (`HALF_UP`).
Rounding happens **per line only**: each discount component and each tax. Totals are sums and are never rounded again, just like the electronic invoice.

The quote is **sealed**: its lines are insert-only and the order stores no amount. Confirming copies what was quoted and never runs the engine again, so a price or lever change cannot reach an open quote.
Credit is checked when quoting, as information (`fits`, `available`, `shortfall`), and consumed when confirming, inside the same transaction.
a1.w1: What is bought triggers the gift, and it never reduces what is paid for a product
a1.w2: The negotiated combo price consumes its units first, so they do not also get a volume discount
a1.w3: The volume incentive applies only to what the combo did not price
a1.w4: Commercial discounts are settled before tax
a1.w5: Tax goes on the base after discounts, plus the gift's value where the country taxes it
a1.l6: Tax per line, at each SKU's rate
a1.w7: It needs every step before it
a1.w8: It needs the final total: informative when quoting, enforced when confirming
a1.tryTitle: Try it: real answers from the engine
a1.tryText: Tienda Norte, Colombia, cash payment. Every figure is the real answer of POST /api/v1/quotes for that cart, recorded on 17 October 2026.

ev.breakdown: Breakdown per line and totals with every field; the total identities hold in every case
ev.order: Levers apply in the documented order; a SKU rule beats a family rule
ev.credit: A credit order says whether it fits the credit line; a total equal to the available amount fits
ev.sealed: The quote is stored insert-only and the order stores no amount
ev.noFloat: No float or double in the domain; rounding per line only; a price with more decimals than its currency is rejected
ev.notHardcoded: The same cart in Colombia (scale 0) and Ecuador (scale 2) follows each country's configuration
ev.gt1: Golden test 1 · two-bracket discount: a 2,750 discount and a 71,103 total
ev.gt2: Golden test 2 · combo: one COMBO entry and no loose discount on its products
ev.gt3: Golden test 3 · gift: it appears as a line with its quantity and origin
ev.gt4: Golden test 4 · combo with taxes: the tax enters the 11,529 total
ev.gt5: Golden test 5 · credit exceeded: fits=false, and confirming answers 409 with no order and no consumption
ev.gt6: Golden test 6 · regression: after a price and a lever change, the confirmed total is the quoted one

a2.title: Idempotent, consistent confirmation
a2.status: Concurrency, failures before and after commit and ERP outages, tested against real PostgreSQL with Testcontainers
a2.quote: In three different releases, an order was confirmed, the shopkeeper got an order number, and then it did not show in their history. POST /orders accepts an idempotency key. If the answer is 201 with an order number, the order exists and can be queried.
how: **One transaction per confirmation**: idempotency key → quote lock → conditional credit consumption → order → outbox events → stored answer → commit. The 201 is sent **only after the commit**.
**The 201 invariant**: the detail and the history read the same primary tables that transaction wrote, so a returned number always points at a committed, readable row.

**Retries**: the same key with the same body returns the stored answer, byte for byte, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; with another body, 422. A failure is not cached: the transaction rolls back and releases the key.

**External effects**: push and ERP leave through an outbox written in the same transaction. A relay sends them outside any transaction, retries with backoff and jitter, and consumers drop duplicates by `event_id`. If the ERP is down, the order stays confirmed and the effect waits.

**Consistency model**: strong inside the database and eventual towards push and ERP. It gives up availability when the database is down, and serializes one customer's confirmations on their credit row.
a2.transcriptText: Real API answers with the same Idempotency-Key. The second body is byte-identical to the first: one order and one credit consumption.

ev.missingKey: A missing or invalid Idempotency-Key answers 400
ev.replay: Same key and same body: a byte-identical answer; another body: 422
ev.concurrency: N concurrent requests with one key create one order and one consumption; of two that together exceed the credit, only one succeeds
ev.alreadyConfirmed: A new key on a confirmed quote answers 409 with the existing number
ev.failure: A failure before commit leaves nothing; after a crash after commit, the retry returns the same number
ev.readable: Every 201 order is readable at once by id and in the history
ev.outboxWrite: A confirmed order produces exactly one push event and one ERP event
ev.outboxRelay: ERP down: retries with backoff and delivery on recovery; re-send after a crash, deduplicated by event_id; DEAD when attempts run out
ev.boundary: Transactions live only in the application layer
ev.model: The consistency model and what it gives up are written in the README and the ADR

a3.title: One-page ADR
a3.status: One A4 page in Spanish and one in English; the documentation check fails above 500 words or when a section is missing
a3.quote: A short document, the kind you would hand to your team: the decisions you took and the alternatives you discarded; what you consciously did not build and why; what you would check in a code review; a risk you see in the design and how you would mitigate it.
how: **Decisions and alternatives**: a sealed quote instead of copying the breakdown or recomputing on confirm; `BigDecimal` per line instead of integers or rounding the total; one PostgreSQL transaction instead of memory, asynchronous writes or a saga; a transactional outbox instead of publishing after commit; a hexagonal monolith instead of microservices.

**Not built, on purpose**: authentication (a gateway would inject tenant and customer), real push and ERP (fakes behind ports), and what was not asked: revocation, cancellation, credit release, catalog, deployment and CI.

**Code-review checklist**: no `float` or `double`; `@Transactional` only in use cases; locks in order and the 201 after commit; the relay with no open transaction; each lever with a golden test seen failing.
**Risk and mitigation**: a sealed quote honors a wrong price until it expires. A 15-minute validity per country contains it, and a review is triggered if an incident touches more than 100 quotes.

ev.adr: The ADR fits one page (500 words or fewer per language) and covers the four requested points

delivery.title: Repository, one command, README and history
delivery.status: test-all green on fresh clones · 82 pull requests merged in 4 phases
delivery.quote: A Git repository with the code and the tests, with one command to run them; a README with how to run it, the lever order, the rounding policy and the consistency model; the ADR; a readable commit history.
how: `orderflow-engine-api` is the deliverable: code, tests, README and ADR. The other repositories go with it: web client, infrastructure, documentation and tools.
One command for everything: `bash orderflow-engine-infra/scripts/test-all.sh`. The API alone: `./mvnw verify`, with the coverage gate.
The README holds the four topics in one file, in English and Spanish, and an automatic check fails if one is missing.
A readable history: one conventional commit per task, each entered through a pull request, and each phase closed with a merge into `main`.

front.title: Angular web client
front.status: 209 specs in headless Chromium · the full flow end to end in Spanish and English
front.quote: An order summary screen: lines, discounts with their origin, gifts with quantity, taxes and total. No text is cut. No control is hidden by the system navigation bar or the keyboard. Images in the same grid scale by the same rule.
how: The requested screen consumes the API's real pricing. At the product owner's request it grew into the full flow: store, catalog, cart, quote, confirmation, order and My orders.

**Prevention at component level**: all text goes through `ui-text`, which wraps and never cuts; the action bar (`ui-action-bar`) respects the safe area and rises with the keyboard; every image goes through `ui-product-image`, with one aspect ratio.
A test fails if a template writes text outside those components, and the specs measure the layout in a real browser at 768 and 375 px.
A double tap on Confirm sends one request and reuses the same key on every retry.
All text lives in Spanish and English dictionaries. The time spent beyond the suggested hour is measured in the API README.

ev.noTruncation: Long names wrap without being cut at 768 and 375 px on every screen
ev.noHidden: The action bar respects the safe area and stays above the keyboard
ev.images: Every image uses the same aspect ratio, and a missing image shows a fallback
ev.prevention: The client README explains prevention at component level
ev.doubleTap: A double tap on Confirm sends one request with one key

countries.title: Countries, brands and languages
countries.status: Four tenants seeded as data only · API and client in Spanish and English
countries.quote: The app runs in several countries (Colombia, Ecuador, Guatemala, Peru, among others) and several commercial brands, on the same multi-tenant platform. Multi-country: currency, decimal scale and rates cannot be hard-coded in the logic.
how: A tenant is country + brand (`co-alpha`, `ec-alpha`, `gt-alpha`, `pe-alpha`). Currency, scale, rounding, the gift tax policy and the quote validity are the country's data.
Guatemala and Peru were added as data only: one Liquibase changelog, without a single line of Java.
Each country numbers its orders with its own sequence (`CO-000001`, `GT-000001`…).
API errors follow `Accept-Language`; the web client switches language without reloading and remembers it.

ev.countryConfig: The same cart in two countries follows each one's scale and rules
ev.seeds: Each tenant sees only its products and numbers its orders with its own sequence
ev.apiLanguage: Errors arrive in the requested language, falling back to Spanish, and every code exists in both languages
ev.webLanguage: The client dictionaries have the same keys, and the language choice survives a reload
